What to do in Saugatuck: Beaches, wineries, and art galleries to know

The region’s largest outdoor draw is Oval Beach, recognized as one of the most beautiful beaches in the country. Pack the umbrella and take in the shoreline activities—visitors and locals alike come here for swimming, sunbathing, and rounds of frisbee. A large parking lot is right next to the beach, helping to ensure a smooth transition from vehicle to vacation mode.

Taste some wine and enjoy the vineyard views at Modales Wines in Fennville. Owners Jim and Carol Gonzalez opened the winery in 2019 with the mission of making local bottles with sustainable practices and world-class vision. Today, they have been recognized as one of Michigan’s only certified organic wineries, with nearly two dozen bottles on offer. Book a guided tasting to sample through several of them, including favorites like the rose, syrah, and the award-winning Sauvignon Blanc or Gruner Veltliner. Pair it up with any of their onsite snacks (especially the goat’s and cow’s milk cheese spreads from nearby Evergreen Lane Farm & Creamery).

Explore the area by water with a Star of Saugatuck cruise, a 90-minute sternwheel ride down the Kalamazoo River and onto Lake Michigan. Enjoy the trip during the daytime, or book a sunset cruise for golden hour photo opps. Near this dock, spot the Saugatuck Chain Ferry, a hand-cranked chain ferry that connects the downtown district to Mount Baldhead Park and Oval Beach (in use since 1838, it is the only remaining chain driven ferry in the country).

Discover the area’s rich arts scene with visits to local galleries, including J. Petter, Dune, and Button Gallery. And check the calendar at Saugatuck Center for the Arts for regularly scheduled concerts, author talks, and artist exhibits (including the recent Mother Lake from local artist Bryanna Manning). During warmer months, swing by the parking lot on Fridays for a weekly farmers market.

Saugatuck has several wonderful downtown shopping options—visit Brass Anchor for women’s clothing and accessories, Leon Footwear for handcrafted footwear, and The Book Nook for many beach read contenders. Spend some time exploring Lulu Cadieux—housed in a historic bank building, the lifestyle boutique celebrates everyday joys through a culinary learning center and thoughtfully curated retail selection. The shop features items across multiple categories, including home, garden, and beauty, and owner Terry Walker plans frequent trips abroad to procure goods (including vintage apparel and accessories). Guests can learn about different cuisines and techniques with the team’s onsite cooking classes, which take place in a spacious, state-of-the-art kitchen (complete with a beautiful cookbook collection). And those seeking more of the shop’s aesthetic and ethos can stay overnight at The Polo Shed, their private guest house. Located a short distance from the shop, the property sleeps up to 12 and features comforts and charms such as feather chandeliers, a grand piano, a stone fireplace, and a chef’s kitchen.
